root_cause_label: Naive Motion Intensity Strategy Fails to Distinguish Jump from Running
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a simplistic motion-intensity thresholding strategy that cannot distinguish the specific hurdle-jump takeoff/landing from the athlete's general running motion throughout the clip.
t_err_evidence: In step 6 the agent adopts a naive strategy: compute total contour area against the first (background) frame and apply a 30% peak threshold to identify takeoff and landing. This is a false premise — the video contains continuous running motion before and after the jump, so the threshold fires on every stride as well, and the 'first frame above threshold' is not the jump takeoff.
t_commit_evidence: In step 7 the agent writes the final jump_analyzer.py implementing exactly this flawed motion-thresholding logic verbatim and no further algorithmic changes are made; the failing strategy is now locked into the deliverable file.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that the first frame above a 30% motion-intensity threshold corresponds to jump takeoff, and the last sustained high-motion frame to landing. This premise is wrong because (a) the athlete is running throughout the clip, causing continuous high-motion frames unrelated to the jump, and (b) the approach cannot isolate the single stride where both feet leave the ground.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6 output shows sustained high motion from frame 46 all the way through frame 72 with no discernible peak that isolates a jump, plus a second blob of motion around frames 100-118 that the agent ignores. A careful reading of these numbers would reveal that frames 48 and 69 are not obviously special jump events.
